key_insight: In a supersonic reacting mixing layer, near-field combustion noise is broadband and burst-driven, with weak but frequency-selective coupling between pressure and heat release rather than a single dominant acoustic mode.
engineering_relevance: This helps guide how to predict and mitigate combustion noise in high-speed reacting flows where source intermittency and low-frequency bias matter more than tonal resonance.
method: High-fidelity time-resolved DNS of a supersonic hydrogen-air temporal mixing layer
Joint analysis of pressure, heat-release, and dilatation fields
Spectral, source-radiation-potential, and information-theoretic measures of coupling
evidence_signal: The DNS shows weak pressure–heat-release coherence in selected low-frequency bands, moderate low-frequency angular bias in the source projection, and stronger statistical similarity between pressure and heat release than between pressure and dilatation.
watch_item: The findings are near-field and source-side; translating them to far-field noise predictions will require observer-based or acoustic-analogy calculations.
paper_title: Near-Field Combustion-Noise Source Dynamics in a Reacting Supersonic Temporal Mixing Layer
